# What the clarify record left open, answered

Jev held `clarified` at 0.77 against 0.8 on the first reading. Four things the record
decided how to build without saying what happens to what is already there.

## Journals written before a record carried a session

Nineteen journals exist and not one record in them carries a session, so sessions per
ticket cannot be counted for them. It reports null, not 1 and not 0: null is the absence
of a count, 1 would be a claim that each of those tickets was worked in a single session,
and that is exactly the claim this ticket was opened because nobody can make. The figure
becomes real for tickets started after this change, SEEN-104 itself first, whose own
journal begins under the old envelope and continues under the new one. Its count is
therefore a lower bound, and the KPI record says so rather than rounding it up.

## Solution records already advanced

The slice plan binds advances from the moment it lands. The nine solution records already
in journals are not revisited and no gate reads them for slices: `gates._tdd` reads a
solution record only for its `mode`, and `latest_evidence` is never asked for a plan. No
ticket is sitting at the solution stage today, so nothing in flight has to be redrafted.

Adding a required key to `harness/templates/solution.json` will fail every test fixture
that builds a solution record, the way `mode` failed fifty-five of them in SEEN-103. That
is the field doing its job. The shared fixture gains a one-slice plan; the non-code tests
keep none, because a non-code record is exempt from the plan exactly as it is exempt from
`tests_first`.

## What the pack calls the current slice

Before the solution record has advanced there is no plan, and the pack says the stage and
that no slice has been accepted yet. After it, the current slice is the first slice in the
plan with no accepted GREEN cited against it in this attempt; when every slice has one,
the pack says the plan is complete and names the review stage as the next stop. The pack
never invents a slice that is not in the plan.

## When the session cannot be identified

`budget` finds this session's log by the session id, so with no id there is no log and
every figure is null, with the reason given. It is the same rule `cost.py` already applies
to a machine with no logs at all: zero is a claim that nothing was spent, and the honest
answer is that nobody knows.
